<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par49" />{{GHGheb|text=יָקֹ֫ם}}, with {{GHGterm|wāw consec.}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיָּ֫קָם|translate=and he arose}} ({{GHGpar|67|n}} and x, {{GHGpar|68|d}}, {{GHGpar|69|p}}, § 71, {{GHGpar|72|t}} and aa, {{GHGpar|73|e}}).<ref>The plural forms in {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} also occur less frequently after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}; cf., however, {{GHGheb|text=וַיְרִיבוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=8|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=11|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=44|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=4|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=5|verse=20|hidebook=1}}. The 2nd fem. sing. in {{GHGheb|text=־ִין}} never occurs after {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}}.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|e}}
In the ''first'' pers. sing. alone the retraction of the tone and even the reducing of the long vowel in the final syllable (''û'' to ''ō'', ''î'' to ''ē'', and then to ''ŏ'' and ''ĕ'') are not usual,<ref>In the 1st plur. {{GHGheb|text=וַנַּֽעֲמִיד}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=3}} is the only instance in which the vowel remains unreduced (cf. {{GHGheb|text=ונשׁוב}}, i.e. {{GHGheb|text=וַנָּשׁוּב}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=4|verse=9|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}; {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} {{GHGheb|text=וַנָּ֫שָׁב}}). On the treatment of the tone in the imperfect, imperative, and infinitive {{GHGterm|Niphʿal}}, see {{GHGpar|51|n}}.</ref> at least according to the Masoretic punctuation, and the apocope in verbs {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} occurs more rarely; e.g. always {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקוּם}} (or {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקֻ֫ם}}, a merely orthographic difference) ''and I arose''; ''Hiph.'' {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקִים}} (but generally written {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקִם}}, implying the pronunciation ''wāʾ{{GHGtranslit|a-macr-acut}}qem'', as {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָקֻם}} implies ''wāʾāqŏm''); {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶרְאֶה|translate=and I saw}}, more frequently than {{GHGheb|text=וָאֵ֫רֶא}}, {{GHGpar|75|t}}. On the other hand, the form with final {{GHGheb|text=־ָה}} is often used in the 1st pers. both sing. and plur., especially in the later books, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶשְׁלְחָה|translate=and I sent}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=43|verse=21|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=8|verse=19}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֶתְּנָה}}, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=2|verse=28}}, and often, probably a sort of compensation for the lost {{GHGheb|text=נ‍}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=6|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=12|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=90|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=55|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=15}} ff., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=19|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=7|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=25|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=2|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=5|verse=7.8.13|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=6|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=13|verse=7–11.21 f.|hidebook=1}}, &c.—Sometimes, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=3|verse=6}}, with a certain emphasis of expression, and probably often, as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=10|verse=12}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאוֹשִׁ֫יעָה}} before {{GHGheb|text=א}}, for euphonic reasons. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=8|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאָעִ֫ידָה}} may have been originally intended; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=16}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲח׳}} and in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=26}} {{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲי׳}}. In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=3|verse=3}} read {{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽכְלֶהָ}} or {{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽכְלָהּ}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|f}}
This {{GHGheb|text=ו·}} is in meaning a strengthened {{GHGterm|wāw copulative}}, and resembles in pronunciation the form which is retained in Arabic as the ordinary copula (''wă'').<ref>In usage the Hebrew {{GHGterm|wāw}} does duty for the Arabic ''fă'' ({{GHGterm|wāw apodosis}}, see {{GHGpar|143|d}}) as well as ''wă''.</ref> The close connexion of this ''wă'' with the following consonant, caused the latter in Hebrew to take {{GHGterm|Dageš}}, especially as ''ă'' could not have been retained in an open syllable. Cf. {{GHGheb|text=בַּמָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּמָּה}}, {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לַמָּה}}), where the prepositions {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=לְ}}, and the particle {{GHGheb|text=כְּ‍}}, are closely connected with {{GHGheb|text=מָה}} in the same way ({{GHGpar|102|k}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|g}}
The retraction of the tone also occurs in such combinations, as in {{GHGheb|text=לָ֫מָּה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לַמָּ֫ה}} {{GHGpar|102|l}}).—The identity of many {{GHGterm|consecutive}} forms with jussives of the same conjugation must not mislead us into supposing an intimate relation between the moods. In the consecutive forms the shortening of the vowel (and the retraction of the tone) seems rather to be occasioned solely by the strengthening of the preformative syllable, while in the jussives the shortening (and retraction) belongs to the character of the form.

{{GHGmargin-letter|49|h}}
'''3.''' The counterpart of {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} is {{GHGterm|wāw consecutive}} of the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, by means of which perfects are placed as<section end="par49" /><noinclude>
